# Cosmic Library user guide

Cosmic Library is a free website about space: simulations you can fly, live data you can explore, and lessons you can learn from. You need nothing but a web browser. **[Open it ↗](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/)**

## The basics

- **Press the <kbd>?</kbd> button** at the top right of any page (or the <kbd>?</kbd> key) for that page's controls and tips (and, on the heavier 3D pages, a *Switch to low graphics* button).
- **3D pages:** drag to look around, scroll or pinch to zoom. Each page's exact controls are below.
- **Slow?** Use *Switch to low graphics* in the help panel where there is one, close other tabs, and plug in your laptop. See the [FAQ](FAQ.md#its-slow).
- **Blank or black page?** Your browser's graphics acceleration (Web Graphics Library, WebGL) is probably off. See the [FAQ](FAQ.md#the-page-is-blank-or-black).
- **No account, no tracking.** A few pages remember settings on your own device. See [privacy](FAQ.md#privacy).

## Home

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/"><img src="../media/screens/home-fly.jpg" alt="Home" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/)** · The front door: a tour of every page, tonight's sky over your city and a zoom from a proton to the universe.

**Try this first**

1. Pick a mood under "Where do you want to start?" and follow the suggested pages.
2. Drag the handle under "Drag from a proton to the universe" to feel the powers of ten.
3. Press "Use my location" to see tonight's sky for where you are (optional; nothing is sent anywhere).

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Click | Open any card or tile |
|  | Drag | Move the zoom handle and the sky time slider |
| **Touch** | Tap | Open any card or tile |
|  | One-finger drag | Move the zoom handle and the sky time slider |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between links and controls |
|  | <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Step the zoom handle when it has focus |
|  | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Open the page for the current zoom stop |

- **Calculated in your browser.** Planet and Moon positions are calculated in your browser from published orbital elements. Nothing on this page is fetched live. *Offline:* Everything works offline once the page has loaded.
- **If it's slow:** This page is light. If it stutters, turn on reduced motion in your system settings: the starfield and meteors stop.
- **On a phone:** yes. Fully usable on phones.

## Fly

Launch, land and design rockets.

### Saturn V launch

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/launch.html"><img src="../media/screens/launch.jpg" alt="Saturn V launch" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/launch.html)** · Ride Apollo 11 from the launch pad to Earth orbit, with live telemetry computed from the real flight report.

**Try this first**

1. Press Launch (or Space) and watch the director camera follow the climb.
2. Try the cameras: 1 Director, 2 Pad, 3 Track, 4 Chase, 5 Onboard, 6 Free.
3. Speed things up with the time-warp buttons or [ and ].
4. Open Telemetry to see speed, altitude and the rocket equation update live.

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Click | Launch, pause, restart, change camera and time warp with the on-screen buttons |
|  | Drag | Orbit the rocket (Free camera only) |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom (Free camera only) |
| **Touch** | Tap | Use the on-screen Launch, camera and warp buttons |
|  | One-finger drag | Orbit the rocket (Free camera only) |
|  | Pinch | Zoom (Free camera only) |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>Space</kbd> | Launch, then pause / resume |
|  | <kbd>R</kbd> | Restart |
|  | <kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>6</kbd> | Cameras: Director, Pad, Track, Chase, Onboard, Free |
|  | <kbd>[</kbd> <kbd>]</kbd> | Slower / faster time warp (1× to 50×) |

- **Simulation.** A physics simulation of the real flight, tuned to the Saturn V Flight Evaluation Report for Apollo 11 (AS-506). *Offline:* Everything is built in your browser, so it works offline.
- **If it's slow:** Open Settings and choose Rendering quality: Low. Your choice is remembered on this device.
- **On a phone:** yes. Works on phones; the telemetry sheet starts folded so the rocket stays in view.
- **Next:** [Booster landing](#booster-landing) · [Rocket builder](#rocket-builder) · [Orbit Lab](#orbit-lab)

<br clear="right">

### Booster landing

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/booster.html"><img src="../media/screens/booster.jpg" alt="Booster landing" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/booster.html)** · Land a reusable first stage on a drone ship or back at the launch site, by hand or with the autopilot.

**Try this first**

1. Pick a scenario (Drone ship, Return to launch site or Final approach).
2. Press "Watch the autopilot" first to see a good landing.
3. Then press "Fly it yourself": W / S throttle, A / D tilt, Space to light the engines, G for legs.
4. Watch the dashed yellow predicted path: land with it on the pad and your speed near zero.

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Drag | Swing the camera around the booster |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom in and out |
|  | Click | Autopilot, ignite, legs, engines, camera and warp buttons |
| **Touch** | One-finger drag | Swing the camera around the booster |
|  | Press and hold | Hold ◀ ▶ to tilt and ▲ ▼ to throttle (flight pad appears while flying) |
|  | Tap | IGNITE, LEGS, AUTO, CAM and warp buttons |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> | Throttle up / down (also ↑ ↓) |
|  | <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | Tilt left / right (also ← →) |
|  | <kbd>Space</kbd> | Start, then ignite / cut the engines |
|  | <kbd>G</kbd> | Landing legs |
|  | <kbd>1</kbd> <kbd>3</kbd> <kbd>9</kbd> | Number of engines |
|  | <kbd>H</kbd> | Retrograde hold |
|  | <kbd>P</kbd> | Autopilot on / off |
|  | <kbd>C</kbd> | Next camera |
|  | <kbd>R</kbd> | Restart |
|  | <kbd>[</kbd> <kbd>]</kbd> | Time warp (1×, 3×, 10×, 30×) |
|  | <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Pause (or close the result card) |

- **Simulation.** A rigid-body flight simulation with a real atmosphere model and published Falcon 9-class numbers. Not live. *Offline:* Works offline.
- **If it's slow:** Open Settings and choose Low, or add ?q=low to the address. Phones start on Low automatically. Low graphics link: [`?q=low`](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/booster.html?q=low).
- **On a phone:** yes. On-screen hold buttons appear while you fly.
- **Next:** [Saturn V launch](#saturn-v-launch) · [Moon landing](#moon-landing) · [Rocket builder](#rocket-builder)

### Moon landing

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/moon-landing.html"><img src="../media/screens/moon-landing.jpg" alt="Moon landing" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/moon-landing.html)** · Fly the Apollo 11 lunar module down to the Sea of Tranquility, or watch Neil Armstrong's real descent.

**Try this first**

1. Choose where to start: the whole descent (Powered Descent Initiation), High Gate or Low Gate.
2. Pick "Watch Armstrong" to see the real flight, or "I'll fly" to try it yourself.
3. Press Begin descent (or Space). Press P to take over by hand for the last few hundred feet.
4. Use ↑ ↓ to change the descent rate by 1 foot per second and ← → to lean forward or back.

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Click | Begin, pause, take over, cameras, warp, and the ▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ pads |
|  | Drag | Orbit the lander (Free camera only) |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom (Free camera only) |
| **Touch** | Tap | Tap ▲ ▼ for descent rate, hold ◀ ▶ to pitch |
|  | One-finger drag | Orbit the lander (Free camera only) |
|  | Pinch | Zoom (Free camera only) |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>Space</kbd> | Begin, then pause / resume |
|  | <kbd>P</kbd> | Take over by hand (P66) / give control back |
|  | <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Descent rate ±1 ft/s (also W / S) |
|  | <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Pitch back / forward, or move the landing point (also A / D) |
|  | <kbd>X</kbd> | Engine off after contact (manual only) |
|  | <kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>6</kbd> | Cameras: Director, Window, Chase, Side, Plot, Free |
|  | <kbd>[</kbd> <kbd>]</kbd> | Time warp (1× to 20×) |
|  | <kbd>R</kbd> | Restart |

- **Simulation.** A guidance and flight simulation checked against the Apollo 11 descent record (including the 1202 and 1201 alarms). *Offline:* Works offline.
- **If it's slow:** Open Settings and choose Low, or add ?q=low to the address. Phones start on Low automatically. Low graphics link: [`?q=low`](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/moon-landing.html?q=low).
- **On a phone:** yes. Use the ▲ ▼ ◀ ▶ pads on screen.
- **Next:** [Moon explorer](#moon-explorer) · [Booster landing](#booster-landing) · [Mars landing](#mars-landing)

### Mars landing

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/mars-landing.html"><img src="../media/screens/mars-landing.jpg" alt="Mars landing" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/mars-landing.html)** · The Perseverance rover's "seven minutes of terror": entry, parachute, powered descent and sky crane, step by step.

**Try this first**

1. Press "Watch the landing" and let the director camera tell the story.
2. Use ← → to jump between events (parachute, heat shield, sky crane…).
3. Press "Why Mars is hard" for a short explainer.
4. Switch to "Be the engineer", change the parachute trigger or crane height, then "Fly my landing".

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Click | Play, restart, speed, cameras and the timeline |
|  | Drag | Scrub the timeline; orbit the spacecraft in the Free camera |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom (Free camera only) |
| **Touch** | Tap | Play, cameras, and events on the timeline |
|  | One-finger drag | Scrub the timeline; orbit in the Free camera |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play / pause |
|  | <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Previous / next event |
|  | <kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>5</kbd> | Cameras: Director, Chase, Side, Ground, Free |
|  | <kbd>E</kbd> | Switch between Watch and Engineer |
|  | <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Close the explainer |

- **Simulation.** A reconstruction of the Mars 2020 entry, descent and landing from published Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) numbers. Your engineer runs are simulated with the same physics. *Offline:* Works offline (event notes come from a local file).
- **If it's slow:** Open Settings and choose Low, or add ?q=low to the address. Low graphics link: [`?q=low`](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/mars-landing.html?q=low).
- **On a phone:** yes. The telemetry sheet starts folded.
- **Next:** [Moon landing](#moon-landing) · [Booster landing](#booster-landing) · [Mission designer](#mission-designer)

### Rocket builder

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/builder.html"><img src="../media/screens/builder.jpg" alt="Rocket builder" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/builder.html)** · Design a rocket from real engines and tanks, check its change in velocity (Δv), then fly it to orbit.

**Try this first**

1. Load a preset from "Load a preset…" to start from a working rocket.
2. Drag a part from Parts onto a stage, or click it to add it to the selected stage.
3. Open Analysis to see where the mass goes and whether you can reach orbit.
4. Press Launch (or Shift + Enter) and watch the flight; press Esc to come back and improve it.

|---|---|---|

|  | Right-drag | Pan (right-drag) |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom |

| **Touch** | Tap | Tap a part to add it to the selected stage |
|  | One-finger drag | Orbit the rocket |
|  | Pinch | Zoom |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> | Undo (⌘ on a Mac) |
|  | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Y</kbd> | Redo (also Ctrl + Shift + Z) |
|  | <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Launch the design |
|  | <kbd>Space</kbd> | Pause / resume the flight |

- **Simulation.** A two-dimensional ascent simulation (real atmosphere, Earth's rotation and gravity) using published engine data. *Offline:* Works offline. Your design lives in the page address, so "Copy link" shares it.
- **If it's slow:** Add ?q=low to the address (phones start on low automatically). Low graphics link: [`?q=low`](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/builder.html?q=low).
- **On a phone:** partly. Works, but building is easier on a larger screen.

### Mission designer

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/mission-designer.html"><img src="../media/screens/mission-designer.jpg" alt="Mission designer" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/mission-designer.html)** · Plan a real interplanetary mission in five steps: destination, launch window, launch vehicle, spacecraft budgets, review.

**Try this first**

1. Pick a destination in step 1 (or a ready-made mission from Presets…).
2. In step 2, click a cool colour on the porkchop plot to choose a cheap launch date.
3. Walk through steps 3–5 with Next and keep an eye on the Margins box.
4. Press any "why?" button for a short explanation.

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Click | Pick a destination, a porkchop cell and the step buttons |
|  | Drag | Rotate the 3D trajectory view |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom the 3D view |
| **Touch** | Tap | Pick a destination, a porkchop cell and the step buttons |
|  | One-finger drag | Rotate the 3D view |

| **Keyboard** | <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> <kbd>↑</kbd> <kbd>↓</kbd> | Move on the porkchop plot or the destination list (when focused) |

|  | <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Close pop-ups |

- **Calculated in your browser.** Trajectories are calculated in your browser (Lambert solutions from planet positions); vehicle and spacecraft numbers come from published sources. *Offline:* Works offline. Your plan is saved in the page address, so you can bookmark or share it.
- **If it's slow:** Add ?q=low to the address for a lighter 3D view. Low graphics link: [`?q=low`](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/mission-designer.html?q=low).
- **On a phone:** partly. Works; the porkchop plot is small on a phone.

## Explore

Live data and 3D worlds, from satellites to galaxies.

### Live Earth orbit

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/earth.html"><img src="../media/screens/earth.jpg" alt="Live Earth orbit" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/earth.html)** · A globe with thousands of real satellites where they are right now, plus upcoming launches and spaceflight news.

**Try this first**

1. Press "Where is the ISS?" (or I) to fly to the International Space Station (ISS).
2. Click any dot to see which satellite it is and draw its orbit.
3. Open the Passes tab and press "Use my location" to see when the ISS flies over you.
4. Speed time up with + and press Now to come back to the present.

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Drag | Spin the globe |
|  | Scroll wheel | Zoom |
|  | Click | Select a satellite |
| **Touch** | One-finger drag | Spin the globe |
|  | Pinch | Zoom |
|  | Tap | Select a satellite |

- **Live data.** Live: orbits from CelesTrak, launches from The Space Devs and news from the Spaceflight News API, cached for a while on your device. *Offline:* If CelesTrak can't be reached, the page builds illustrative constellations from a local file and says so. Add ?offline to see that mode.
- **If it's slow:** No quality switch here. Turn off Labels and Clouds in the Satellites tab, and close other tabs.
- **On a phone:** yes. The panel becomes a bottom sheet.

### Night sky

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/sky.html"><img src="../media/screens/sky.jpg" alt="Night sky" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/sky.html)** · A planetarium for any place and time: stars, planets, the Moon and constellations as they are above you tonight.

|  | <kbd>M</kbd> <kbd>P</kbd> <kbd>K</kbd> | Messier objects, planet labels, ecliptic |
|  | <kbd>Z</kbd> <kbd>E</kbd> <kbd>G</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> | Alt-azimuth grid, equatorial grid, ground, atmosphere |
|  | <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Close the info card |

- **Calculated in your browser.** Calculated in your browser from a real star catalogue (Hipparcos, via d3-celestial) and standard astronomy formulas. Nothing is fetched live. *Offline:* Works offline. "Use my location" asks your browser once and keeps the answer on the page only.
- **If it's slow:** No quality switch: the page lowers its own resolution when frames are slow. Turning off Atmosphere (A) and Twinkling also helps.
- **On a phone:** yes. Made for holding up to the real sky.

- **Live data.** Images load from NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia servers (hotlinked, not copied). APOD comes live from NASA's API. *Offline:* Offline the stories still show; images are marked unavailable and the APOD section hides.
- **If it's slow:** Images load as you scroll; a slow connection just fills in more slowly.
- **On a phone:** yes. Swipe in the viewer.
- **Next:** [Timeline](#timeline) · [Solar observatory](#solar-observatory) · [Sky surveys](#sky-surveys)

### Telescope simulator

<a href="https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/eyepiece.html"><img src="../media/screens/eyepiece.jpg" alt="Telescope simulator" width="360" align="right"></a>

**[▶ Open it](https://normansrule.github.io/cosmic-library/eyepiece.html)** · See what binoculars, a telescope or a camera would really show you of the Moon, planets and deep-sky objects from your sky tonight.

**Try this first**

1. Pick an instrument in step 1, or set your own aperture and focal length.
2. Pick an eyepiece in step 2; tick the 2× Barlow lens to double the power.
3. Pick a target that is up now in step 3 and look at "What you get".
4. In step 5, set the air steadiness, light pollution (Bortle class) and minutes in the dark.
5. Tick "Compare two instruments" and try "70 mm vs 8-inch".

<br clear="right">

| | Do this | To |
|---|---|---|
| **Mouse** | Click | Choose instrument, eyepiece, target and sky |
|  | Drag | Move around a target bigger than the field of view |
|  | Double-click | Re-centre the view |
| **Touch** | Tap | Choose instrument, eyepiece, target and sky |
|  | One-finger drag | Move around a target bigger than the field of view |
| **Keyboard** | <kbd>←</kbd> <kbd>→</kbd> | Step through the instruments, eyepieces or targets (when that row has focus) |
|  | <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Move between the steps and controls |

- **Calculated in your browser.** Tonight's sky is calculated in your browser; the view is modelled from the optics (aperture, focal length, eyepiece), the steadiness of the air, light pollution and how dark-adapted your eyes are. *Offline:* Works offline. "Use my location" asks your browser once and keeps the answer on the page only.
- **If it's slow:** This page draws on a light 2D canvas and only redraws the view when you change something. Close other tabs if it stutters.
- **On a phone:** yes. The steps stack into one column.
- **Next:** [Use a telescope](#use-a-telescope) · [Night sky](#night-sky) · [Sky surveys](#sky-surveys)

## Build

Hands-on experiments you can make.

### Experiments

|  | Pinch | Zoom a 3D part |

|  | <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Jump to that build's card |

- **Calculated in your browser.** Builds, parts and 3D files are stored with the site. *Offline:* Works offline; shop links need the internet.
